description: Main window: session commands, reloading profiles and opening the profile file, taskbar flash and badge, program updates as sessions, workspace and scrollback, whether the previous run quit cleanly, notes (private and shared project notes, including turning shared notes on and unlocking them), folder dialog, clipboard text, pasting a clipboard image as a saved file, opening the detached side panel window (fixed label and URL, remembered size and place), desktop notifications, the CPU and memory of each session's process tree, the machine's CPU, memory and GPU for the system bar, whether the machine runs on battery for the power saving mode, push to the phone (ntfy or Pushover settings with secrets in the keychain, a test push, a push for a session's new state), git branches and changes, the repository each session's folder belongs to for the project overview (read from .git without running git), the user's own commit activity for the calendar in the empty window, the work log of working phases and the daily review built from it, the commit history (one page of commits and the changes of one commit), staging, unstaging, discarding and committing the files of a session's repository (by session ID), the timeline of a session's work tree (binding the session's workspace key, taking a silent snapshot after an agent step, listing the snapshots, the changes of one step, going back to one after saving the current state, and deleting them once the session is closed; by session ID), opening a local dev server address a session printed in the browser, paths and web addresses clicked in the terminal (whether a local absolute path is a file or folder, opening it in the file manager or its default program with runnable files only revealed, plain http(s) addresses in the browser), the file tree of a session's folder (listing one folder at a time, never leaving it, and a bounded index of its paths for the filter) and opening one of its files in a read-only viewer window (fresh label, fixed URL and size), worktrees and the worktree cleanup (listing the worktrees Hangar created, their size, removing or pruning one after checking it again), the agent arena (one worktree per contestant, its changes against the shared commit, the user's test command there as an argv array with a time limit, taking the winner over into the project folder uncommitted, discarding a losing arena worktree), local claims (overlaps between the user's own sessions), which sessions wait for an agent's permission or input dialog as its report-only hooks tell and that the person answered one, the agent gate (answering an agent's held edit or shell command, listing and deleting the standing answers, switching the command guard and reading its rules file's summary), profile editing and keychain secrets, session export and the session report (the agent's transcript as Markdown), notification area icon and showing the window, read-only sub-agent view, the context meter of the sessions, the Hangar account (sign-in, projects, the signed-in person's profile picture, opening its own pages and the self-hosting guide, testing the connection to the chosen server), the team connection (sharing a project, confirming new devices and this device's own admission, removing another of the person's own devices, linking repositories, the sessions' states for the team's presence, reserving tasks and answering release requests), the security switches, the queued messages, the protected settings (paste warning, automatic updates, HANGAR.md, snippets), the workspace templates, the partner projects and the cross-project messages between their sessions (linking and unlinking two existing project folders under short names, the sessions of a partner project, the checked and cleaned text to paste into one of them, the messages agents sent with hangar-send that wait for the person: listing them, the checked text to paste into a running agent session of the partner project, and closing one once pasted or discarded), the link groups of running agent sessions (the groups, the sessions that can be linked and the messages between members, linking chosen sessions, unlinking and editing a group's member names and its ask-first toggle, the checked text of one message claimed for one paste, holding one for a click, closing one once pasted or discarded, and telling that the person typed into a member, and the group's history of the last messages delivered or discarded, kept in memory until the group ends), and the start and notice preferences (start mode, last program, folders, session restore, notices; kept by the backend for this window alone), handing the detached panel the one session it may address, taking the results of finished update sessions, local dictation (microphone on while a key is held, speech recognition on this machine, downloading and removing the speech model after consent, taking each dictated text once), the sub-agent definitions of Claude Code and Codex CLI (listing the global ones and those of named project folders, saving a pasted or loaded one as a global Claude Code definition without replacing one unasked, deleting a global one, opening one in the default editor, setting the model or reasoning effort of one definition, only that field, a project's file only after a question and only in folders the backend knows), the copies of the user's Claude Code definitions in Codex CLI (written to ~/.codex/agents and to untracked files of those names in the known projects' .codex/agents, the replaced files kept as .bak), the protected sub-agent settings (the default model per program for every session Hangar starts, the switch per program for the copies) and their figures (a built-in figure or an own PNG, GIF, WebP or JPEG image checked by its bytes, or the clipboard's image), the anonymous usage statistics (the person's answer, the snapshot of the allowlisted settings, counting a named feature, opening the public field list), updates and restart
